newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl meets allies to talk about budget, gold.
newsitem.headline: Kohl meets allies to talk about budget, gold.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl began a meeting with top officials from his centre-right coalition on Sunday evening to discuss projected budget shortfalls and also likely to focus on a plan to revalue gold and currency reserves.

The meeting in Kohl's chancellery was expected to concentrate on how to fill holes in the 1998 budget. Officials going into the meeting, including Finance Minister Theo Waigel, did not comment on the evening's agenda.

Waigel will have to cope with 15 billion marks ($8.8 billion) less in tax income than originally projected next year, and spending is also likely to be higher than hoped because of record post-war unemployment.
He declined to comment on Saturday on reports he will use the meeting to propose a rise in fuel tax or a postponement in a planned reduction of an income tax surcharge.

Kohl's coalition partners, the liberal Free Democrats (FDP), have repeatedly said they will not approve tax hikes to plug holes in the budget and have indicated the future of the coalition would be at stake if Waigel insisted on tax rises.
Officials said the evening meeting was not likely to produce any final decisions.

The battle between Bonn and the Bundesbank over Waigel's plan to revalue gold and currency reserves this year, which has dominated German political debate over the past few days, also looked certain to be discussed at some stage. ($ = 1.705 German Marks)
